record_type_quote: Given the scientific and societal importance of these findings, it is essential to assess their replicability and generalizability, and to investigate the robustness of the results to experimental design choices. To that end, we conceptually replicated Study 4 in Effron & Raj (2020), with an expanded and updated set of headlines, and with an additional set of analyses exploring potential moderating effects of a more ecologically valid environment.

targets.title: Misinformation and morality: encountering fake-news headlines makes them seem less unethical to publish and share.
targets.evidence_quote: To that end, we conceptually replicated Study 4 in Effron & Raj (2020), with an expanded and updated set of headlines, and with an additional set of analyses exploring potential moderating effects of a more ecologically valid environment.
targets.outcome_quote: Given this important result, we replicated the study conducted by Effron & Raj (2020) using an expanded headline set and a larger sample. We successfully replicated the finding that repeated exposure decreases moral condemnation, and found evidence that the effect generalizes across items and samples.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly confirm the central moral-condemnation effect. Auxiliary exploratory outcomes are outside the designed central test.

reasoning: New participants conceptually retest the published moral-condemnation finding in Study 4; reference-list works used for stimuli or theoretical background are not additional targets.
